output.methodChoice: Evidence-ledger provenance check (VP email, vendor certificates and scorecard are interested sources); specification of where failures are and are not (valve source, installer, firmware); then competing-hypotheses weighing of the five explanations.
output.brief:
The evidence points at Pellacott's valves, not the installers or the firmware. Brenmoor's lab matched failures to valve lot, installer and firmware. Pellacott 2026 valves fail at about the same rate (about 41–42 per 1,000) for old and new installers and for both firmware versions. Durrant-Hale valves stay at 5–7 per 1,000 in every group. A helium retest of never-installed Pellacott 2026 stock found 11% leaking at the seat. The independent calibration visit found the leak-test rig out of service since January 2026, with no VA-220 test program on the other rigs. The per-piece certificate tables repeat four fixed sequences, some already in Nov 2025. So the certificates, and the score rise built on them, don't reflect real tests. Pellacott's score is therefore not evidence of quality.

Next steps: keep the six lots on hold and quarantine 2026-built Pellacott stock. Suspend dock-to-stock and run your own helium testing. Do not release lots on fresh certificates. Do not penalise installers. Plan for the line stoppage and add Durrant-Hale supply. Require rig logs or witnessed tests in scoring, and check other suppliers. Don't order a seal reversion yet: the seal change and the new line can't be told apart. Confidence is high on the main finding.
